rules.key: a Veteran Rogue Trader must be assigned to a Rogue Trader cruiser
rules.text: If a fleet has more than one Rogue Trader cruiser or also includes more than one squadron of transports, a Veteran Rogue Trader must be assigned to a Rogue Trader cruiser.
rules.why: The placement is done at the table; the condition also depends on the number of transport skwadrons.

rules.key: Any fleet except Necrons or Tyranids may include a single Rogue Trader capital ship
rules.text: Any fleet except Necrons or Tyranids may include a single Rogue Trader capital ship.
rules.why: 1.1 (14.9.2026): the ROGUE TRADERS section was added to 21 lists. The Tau, Demiurg and Imperial lists get a per_points rule (one per 750 p or part), the others cap 1. Left out are the Necrons and the tyranids (the book's 'except'), the Rogue Trader lists themselves, Bakka / Tau Commerce Protection / Demiurg (their own more specific rule) and the Crusade and the Grey Knights (their own ban, p.99 and p.155). The row is the Rogue Trader Cruiser; the Exploration list's variants are a case of their own. The last sentence ('always count against cruiser restrictions') holds through section_count's pick. Concerns the fleet the Rogue Trader is attached to, not this list.

rules.key: one Rogue Trader cruiser for every 750 points or part thereof
rules.text: Tau, Demiurg and Imperial fleets may include one Rogue Trader cruiser for every 750 points or part thereof in their fleet.
rules.why: 1.1 (14.9.2026): the ROGUE TRADERS section was added to 21 lists. The Tau, Demiurg and Imperial lists get a per_points rule (one per 750 p or part), the others cap 1. Left out are the Necrons and the tyranids (the book's 'except'), the Rogue Trader lists themselves, Bakka / Tau Commerce Protection / Demiurg (their own more specific rule) and the Crusade and the Grey Knights (their own ban, p.99 and p.155). The row is the Rogue Trader Cruiser; the Exploration list's variants are a case of their own. The last sentence ('always count against cruiser restrictions') holds through section_count's pick. Concerns the host fleet (Tau, Demiurg, Imperial). Links between lists are not in v1's model; on the Tau Commerce list the matching rule is enforced with its own rows.

rules.key: Rogue Trader cruisers always count against cruiser restrictions
rules.text: Rogue Trader cruisers always count against cruiser restrictions in any fleet list that has such restrictions.

rules.key: Heavy transports may not be in squadrons with other transport types
rules.text: Heavy transports may not be in squadrons with other transport types.
rules.why: The skwadron's composition is decided at the table.

rules.key: A single squadron of 2-6 Rogue Trader escorts and auxiliary vessels
rules.text: A single squadron of 2-6 Rogue Trader escorts and auxiliary vessels may accompany each Rogue Trader capital ship in a fleet, in any mix desired.
rules.why: The size 2-6 is a squadron rule. On 10.9.2026 (fleet spot check S2, report 17) a ratio was added from the same sentence: at most six escorts per RT ship, cargo ships excluded ('these squadrons can only contain cargo ships'), the Havoc as an escort and the Siluria as a ship following Nate Montes's remark. A mixed squadron ('in any mix desired') cannot be expressed in the unit model, so the number of squadrons is not enforced.

rules.key: Xenos vessels cannot be used in fleets that include Space Marine ships
rules.text: Xenos vessels cannot be used in fleets that include Space Marine ships.
rules.why: A conditional ban, depends on the host fleet's contents.

rules.key: For every 750 points in the fleet, Rogue Traders may be accompanied by a single Demiurg or Kroot vessel
rules.text: For every 750 points in the fleet, Rogue Traders may be accompanied by a single Demiurg or Kroot vessel unless the fleet is using auxiliary ships that cannot be allies with the Demiurg or Kroot (such as Space Marines).
rules.why: 1.1 (14.9.2026): the section got rows and a rule. 750 is read as full, because the sentence does not say 'or part thereof' - unlike the RT cruiser rule on p.184, which does. The ships come from other lists; this list does not have their rows. On the Exploration list the Kroot Warsphere is enforced.

rules.key: Any game that includes a Rogue Trader cruiser must include a sub-plot
rules.text: Any game that includes a Rogue Trader cruiser must include a sub-plot from ... p.82-84 in the Rulebook.

rules.key: may roll randomly against the Xenotech System table below for +15 points per cruiser
rules.text: Each Rogue Trader vessel may roll randomly against the Xenotech System table below for +15 points per cruiser or +5 points per escort. For an additional +5 points per ship, the player can select the desired technology instead of rolling randomly for it.
rules.why: Priced options; the rows 'Xenotech System, rolled randomly (cruiser) 15 pts', 'Xenotech System, rolled randomly (escort, per ship) 5 pts' and 'Choose the Xenotech System instead of rolling 5 pts / ship' can be chosen. Spot check 6: before, one row offered escorts the cruiser's price of 15; the Heavy Transport (p.192, its own +10 refit) and the Xenos Vessel hulls (p.194-198, xenotech included) do not get the list's rows.

rules.key: Auxiliary vessels in a Rogue Trader escort squadron can only use these refits
rules.text: Auxiliary vessels in a Rogue Trader escort squadron can only use these refits if they are in a squadron that includes at least three Rogue Trader escorts.

rules.key: each Rogue Trader cruiser and escort squadron may roll one random crew skill
rules.text: To represent this each Rogue Trader cruiser and escort squadron may roll one random crew skill on ... in the Remastered Rulebook for +10% point value.
rules.why: A percentage price: the rows 'Crew skill, rolled randomly (cruiser / escort squadron, +10% of its points)' can be chosen, and the app computes 10 % of the unit's points before the crew skill, rounded up (J44, 11.9.2026; base and rounding T27). The table is Rulebook p.159.

rules.key: If both players agree before the game, these ships can be included in a Rogue Trader fleet
rules.text: Siluria Class Light Cruisers and Havoc Class Frigates are older, outdated ships ... If both players agree before the game, these ships can be included in a Rogue Trader fleet, as a cruiser and an escort respectively.
rules.why: An agreement between the players; the rows can be chosen in their own section.

extra_entries.name: Xenos Vessel - Pthuxutl war cruiser
extra_entries.why: The named Xenos Vessel variants on the book's pages 196-198, all 50 pts. The book says 'all of them cost 50 points'; the app offers them separately so the card shows the right xenotech system.

notes: Pages 178-183 are narrative (Durandal Grohe, Memet Poralius, Behemoth). They were hidden in the LORE_SECTIONS table: all seven sentences were story.
This list is attachable by nature like the Inquisition: most limits concern the fleet the Rogue Trader is attached to, not this list. That is why only two rules are enforced.

'Auxiliary vessels (pg. 201)' is priced 'varies' - the ship is chosen from another fleet list. The app does not offer the row as an upgrade (10.9.2026, spot check 4): p.201 is a list rule, and the ships are picked from the list of the fleet they escort.
